label: v2
title: A bigger forecast desk.
summary: v2 adds a mesoscale workspace, a workspace-based forecast menu, a cleaner severe-discussion editor, and a new home for pricing and release notes.

sections.title: The Mesoscale workspace
sections.body: A new workspace for the hours before the storms. Browse HRRR, RAP, and RRFS model fields by run and forecast hour, then draw your own mesoscale areas on top and write the discussion that goes with them.
bullets: CAPE, helicity, composite reflectivity, and more, with readable layer names.
Polygons, circles, ellipses, and corridors with forecaster hazard styling you can reshape vertex by vertex.
MRMS radar and GOES satellite context beneath your areas, with freshness labels.

screenshots.alt: The Mesoscale workspace with model fields and drawn areas
screenshots.caption: Model fields by run and forecast hour, with your own areas on top.

sections.title: Forecast workspaces
sections.body: Forecasts now belong to a workspace. The Forecast menu shows each one with a description, so you can jump between severe outlooks, custom layers, and mesoscale analysis without losing your place.
bullets: Autosave, session restore, and cloud saves follow the workspace you are in.
The Cloud Library organizes saved forecasts with workspace tabs and shareable links.
Existing saved cycles, layers, and exports keep working.

screenshots.alt: A severe outlook open in a forecast workspace
screenshots.caption: Autosave, restore, and cloud saves follow the workspace you are in.

sections.title: A calmer severe discussion
sections.body: Edit the severe map and your discussion side by side. Switch between Map, Discussion, and Review / Export, open the discussion full width or in a resizable side panel, and flip between Edit and Preview on narrow screens.

screenshots.alt: The severe discussion editor beside its live preview
screenshots.caption: Edit the map and the discussion side by side.

sections.title: One home for everything
sections.body: gfcweather.com is now the home of Graphical Forecast Creator: what it does, pricing, release notes, and ways to reach us. The app itself lives at app.gfcweather.com, and your old links keep working.

sections.title: Better feedback, safer accounts
sections.body: Send bugs, ideas, and questions from the Resources menu, and know exactly what is collected. Billing redirects are validated, internal errors stay out of what you see, and dependencies were updated to patched versions throughout.

improvements.text: Verification grades archived days against SPC-filtered storm reports only, and shows zero misses when no reports exist instead of a 100% miss rate.
Monitor keeps your last radar frames visible when a refresh fails and tells you when alert polygons were last fetched.
Forecast, verification, and monitor maps use OpenStreetMap, and the map theme applies to state outlines.
Forecast geometry editing is more forgiving: malformed shapes are rejected before snapping, and multi-vertex edits undo as one step.
Keyboard focus stays inside open dialogs, and pages recover on their own from stale cached files.
More than 400 other changes landed in this cycle: fixes, polish, performance work, and quality-of-life improvements across every workspace.

title: The biggest update yet.
summary: A bigger, more connected way to make forecasts, test your thinking, and build the products you actually want to use.

heroImage.alt: Verification v2 Forecast Grade workspace with observed reports and a score breakdown
heroImage.caption: Verification v2 turns a finished forecast into a structured learning session.

sections.title: Verification v2
sections.body: Forecasting is only half the work. Verification v2 gives you a dedicated place to compare what you forecast with what actually happened, so every event becomes a chance to sharpen your judgment.
bullets: Source-aware evidence from SPC storm reports and NOAA Damage Assessment Toolkit surveys.
Report-quality checks, event capture, severity intent, and spatial scoring that show where a forecast worked—or missed.
Probability skill, false-alarm discipline, score breakdowns, shareable summaries, and grade trends over time.

sections.title: Custom Products
sections.body: Make the forecast product you wish existed. Custom Products let you draw your own areas, define meaningful categories, and keep the style consistent from the map to the export.
bullets: Local custom layers and reusable hosted products with category styling, snapshots, exports, and imports.
Built-in Rainfall and Tropical AOI products are available to every account tier and do not use personal product slots.
Owner-scoped storage and premium boundaries keep hosted products useful without blurring who owns them.

screenshots.alt: Custom Products forecast map showing Rainfall and Tropical AOI product styling
screenshots.caption: Custom Products make room for the forecasts that do not fit a standard outlook.

sections.title: Forecast workflows that hold together
sections.body: v1.7 gives a forecast a clearer beginning, middle, and end. Start from a reusable workflow, keep each discussion attached to the right outlook, review the package, and carry it through save, load, export, import, and handoff.
bullets: Versioned workflow packages with scoped discussion and draft persistence.
Review and completion flows that surface missing work before you call a forecast finished.
Handoff guidance, lifecycle metrics, and same-cycle update support for forecasts that keep evolving.

screenshots.alt: Forecast workflow workspace showing an outlook map, review package action, and discussion pane
screenshots.caption: A forecast package now carries its map, discussion, review, and next step together.

sections.title: Auto-TSTM
sections.body: Auto-TSTM uses SPC-calibrated HREF guidance to create a reviewable starting point for categorical work. Preview it, decide what belongs in your forecast, and keep control of the final map.
bullets: Preview, apply, cancel, and undo flows instead of silent map changes.
Cache health and stale-result protection make upstream guidance easier to trust.
Unavailable and server-capability states are explicit across supported release targets.

screenshots.alt: Forecast map with Auto-TSTM tools visible in the toolbar
screenshots.caption: Auto-TSTM helps you get to a thoughtful categorical starting point faster.

sections.title: Monitor and reference data
sections.body: Monitor keeps radar, satellite, alerts, storm reports, and your forecast in one live workspace. v1.7 adds an opt-in SPC mesoscale discussion reference layer with attribution, valid-time state, and bounded caching.
bullets: Source metadata stays visible so reference data remains explainable.
Refresh, retry, stale-data, and phone-layout behavior are more resilient.

sections.title: Privacy and account safety
sections.eyebrow: A clearer boundary around your data
sections.body: The v1.7 privacy update makes the local-first promise more explicit and separates essential account operation from optional measurement. Your forecasts remain yours whether you sign in or stay offline.
bullets: Local forecasts, preferences, and cycle history stay on your device unless you choose hosted sync.
Non-essential product analytics are disabled by default, require separate opt-in, and can be withdrawn at any time.
Beta and production telemetry use separate reporting zones; analytics do not receive account identity, forecast contents, coordinates, filenames, or export contents.
Account deletion now requires recent authentication, cleans up hosted data and billing state, and leaves local offline forecasts untouched.

sections.title: The quiet work underneath
sections.body: There is a lot in this release that does not fit neatly into a poster. v1.7 also hardens the surfaces you use every day—from importing a saved forecast to opening a map on a phone.
bullets: Bounded, schema-validated forecast imports and safer handling of legacy saved shapes.
Auto-categorical recovery that preserves the last known-good result when geometry work fails or times out.
Keyboard, dialog, toolbar, map popup, session restore, and responsive-control improvements across the app.
TypeScript 7 tooling, expanded E2E coverage, dependency/license gates, release manifests, rollback support, and explicit target exposure for local, beta, staging, and production.

improvements.text: Prototype and source-limited evidence remains labeled clearly; NOAA DAT damage points supplement official verification evidence rather than replacing it.
Error monitoring remains separate from product analytics, with environment tags and payload minimization on hosted deployments.
Core forecasting and learning workflows remain free; premium is reserved for hosted capabilities that carry an operating cost.
The release is exposed deliberately across local, beta, staging, and production, with emergency disable controls and server capability boundaries where needed.
